frame.camera: ADR-0006/0022 — ¾ from the south, elev 40°, orthographic
frame.sort: painter, descending world y (north draws first); sortBias breaks ties
frame.pivots: cell pivot is top-left origin; unityPivot is normalised bottom-left

terrain.note: row 0 = north edge. 0 = no tile (water — never baked, the shader owns it). Runs are [value, count]; sum(count) == cols * rows exactly.
terrain.x-waterDatum: metres relative to chart datum — the same datum the height map's elevations use, so elevation and water level are directly comparable. TideModel.Height is `MeanLevel + amplitude * carrier`; this is MeanLevel.

x-tide.x-note: given so a tide-aware wash can swing; the exporter states the model's declared terms and does not evaluate it (no time, and rule 5 says the tide is recomputed, never stored).

ground.label: Ground
ground.x-derived: an iso-contour of the painted height map at the shore map's DECLARED band floors. Coarser than what Unity paints, which additionally wiggles the elevation, tests a sandbar spine and picks a band table by weather sector. Those are logic, not declarations, and reimplementing them here would be a second coastline.

road.label: Road
road.x-derived: stroked from the region's declared route table at each way's declared half-width and rank. Surface material only — the blob-47 tile index stays derived in the one place the repo derives it.

cliff.label: Cliff
cliff.x-derived: not painted; the repo's cliffs are placed surfaces and ship as entities.
cliff.x-unavailable: Cliffs are placed surfaces (CliffWallSurface components), not painted cells. They are exported as entities, where they are authored.

pieces.note: per-cell ledge piece laid by cliff lines; 0 = autotile from neighbours

x-heightField.units: metres relative to chart datum — the same datum as terrain.waterLevelMeters
x-heightField.order: row-major, row 0 = north edge, one sample per stride cell centre
x-heightField.x-note: a shading wash, not a survey: nearest texel at a coarse stride, no interpolation. null means the sample fell outside the painted map. The full-resolution source is terrain.x-heightMap, pinned by textureSha256.

collision.note: Derived, never authored. This export ships no collision sidecars: colliders in the committed scene are builder output, and the shapes that carry gameplay law (quay faces, dock zones, passages) are owned by the region builder rather than by any document.

entityNotes.x-unresolvedMeaning: no sidecar beside these sheets names a rig this exporter will trust — an ambiguous one names several. The kits that ship a *.contract.json resolve exactly; the rest have no committed link from sheet to rig, so nothing is pinned rather than guessed.
entityNotes.x-familyVocabulary: `family` is the editor's own wire vocabulary, transcribed at docs/tools/reference/family-names.json and matched EXACTLY: a rig whose name does not land on a listed one keeps the sprite stem, flags x-familyIsSpriteStem, and appears under unlistedFamilies with the candidate name — never aliased onto a near neighbour. wharfIsoRig normalises to `wharf` and the list holds both `wharfbuilding` and `wharfmodule`; guessing between them is the aliasing the ruling forbids. Those entries are the request list for the editor side.
entityNotes.x-absentEntityFields: facing, facingIndex and gameplaySidecar are named by the format and absent here. The first two are the editor's own view state; the third is a rig gameplay measurement. A baked sprite records none of them, and no rig is executed by this exporter.
entityNotes.x-noCallRecord: call/opts are absent by ruling: the editor writes them out of its own live state and no renderer reads one back. The cost is that this document can never seed a round-trip INTO the editor, which needs family+dir+opts.
